problem: Most VLN models encode the instruction as a static global representation, and existing sub-instruction methods are text- or map-driven, so sub-instructions can activate before their referents are visible or linger after they leave view.
motivation: Instruction meaning depends on what the agent currently sees: landmarks matter only once they enter view, and token importance shifts as context changes. Modeling the instruction as a state that evolves with perception should improve decisions and path efficiency, especially for long compositional instructions.
key_idea: Treat the instruction as a token-level latent state updated at every step: CGIP picks the sub-instruction grounded in the current panorama, and FGIP refines that segment's tokens via cross-attention to the observation and gated fusion.
insight: Both stages matter and are complementary. In the REVERIE ablation, CGIP-only mainly cuts trajectory length (Val Seen TL 10.83), FGIP-only mainly raises SR (Val Seen 73.01), and the full model is best on Val Unseen (SR 48.37, SPL 35.70 vs 34.11 and 33.95). The gains are mostly efficiency (SPL, TL) rather than SR. Plugging the module into HAMT, NavGPT2 and VLN-GOAT gives small but consistent R2R gains of +1 to +2 SR.
method: Instruction-as-State formulation: S_t = f(S_{t-1}, S_0, I, V_t), where S_0 is the full-instruction encoder output. CGIP uses the stable S_0 to avoid error accumulation, while FGIP updates the evolving S_{t-1}.

Sub-Instruction Generator: rule-based clause segmentation on conjunctions and punctuation, followed by a learnable boundary scorer (MLP over neighbouring token features, coarse-boundary prior and coherence cue) trained without boundary annotations.

Sub-Instruction Picker: cross-attention of S_0 over the panoramic tokens V_t gives token relevance r. Relevance is aggregated per clause with within-clause normalized token weights into phi, then softmax gives alpha_t, and top-1 routing selects k* (straight-through gradient in training).
Instruction Refiner (FGIP): cross-attention from the activated tokens S_{t-1}[T_k*] to V_t, then a lightweight Transformer encoder, then scatter back to the original token positions.
Gated fusion: S_t = S_{t-1} + g ⊙ (R_t - S_{t-1}), with g computed by a two-layer MLP over LayerNorm'd S_{t-1} and R_t, to prevent semantic drift.
Training: built on DUET (frozen ViT-B/16 panoramic tokens), trained end-to-end with IL cross-entropy plus A2C RL, L = L_RL + λ L_IL.

setting.backbone: DUET (trained, with S-EGIU plug-in); also HAMT, NavGPT2, VLN-GOAT with S-EGIU
setting.training_data: Standard dataset-specific DUET training recipe on R2R, SOON and REVERIE; no extra data reported (Adam lr 1e-5, 20k steps, RTX 3090)
setting.observation: 36-view panoramic RGB (frozen ViT-B/16 tokens) plus DUET topological map
setting.action_space: discrete navigable viewpoints on a nav graph

results: On REVERIE, S-EGIU beats DUET on SPL: Val Unseen 35.70 vs 33.73 and Test Unseen 38.74 vs 36.06, with shorter trajectories. Test-unseen SR (51.92) and OSR (54.63) are below DUET (52.51 / 59.61). On R2R it gets SR 74 / SPL 61 on val-unseen (DUET 72 / 60). On SOON it raises SPL (24.95 val-unseen, 23.61 test-unseen) at slightly lower SR than DUET. It also outperforms five distilled DUET plug-ins on SPL.
limitations: Gains are modest and mostly in path efficiency (SPL, TL); SR, OSR and RGSPL sometimes fall below DUET, especially on SOON and REVERIE test-unseen.

Relies on sub-instruction boundary quality and on panoramic tokens; sensitive to viewpoint ambiguity and domain shift, and prone to clause-selection errors and drift accumulation in unseen or long-horizon settings.
Baselines are DUET-era; the plug-in comparisons are the authors' own distilled reimplementations, not the original systems, and there is no comparison with recent LLM-based or stronger VLN methods.
